turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Hi doctor—I've had progressive pain in my left leg for about two months, and lately it’s been keeping me from sleeping. It started after I got hit in the thigh by a baseball, and I had redness and swelling for a few days afterward, but the ibuprofen hasn’t helped.”
Do you feel any firm lump or mass in your thigh where you were hit, and has it been increasing in size since the injury?

“Doctor, I don’t think I feel a firm lump exactly where I was hit, but the area feels kind of tender and the pain seems to be getting worse over time. I haven’t noticed any clear swelling coming back or growing in size.”
Have you experienced any fevers, unexplained weight loss, or night sweats over these past two months?
“No, doctor—I haven’t had any fevers, and I haven’t noticed weight loss or night sweats. It’s mostly just the worsening left leg pain that keeps me up at night.”
Do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your left leg, or does the pain radiate anywhere (like down to your knee or up to your hip/groin)?
“No numbness or tingling, and I don’t feel weakness, but the pain does seem to spread a bit down the left thigh toward the knee—mostly staying on that side.”
How old are you, and have you had any X-rays or other imaging of your thigh since this injury occurred?
“I’m 13 years old, and I haven’t had any X-rays or other imaging of my thigh yet.”
Is the pain deep in the bone of your thigh, or does it feel more like it’s in the muscle? And do you limp or have trouble putting full weight on that leg when walking?
“Doctor, it feels more deep and inside the thigh bone than just in the muscle, and I do find myself limping a bit—putting full weight on that leg hurts, especially when I walk for a while.”

Can you point to one specific spot on your thigh bone that hurts the most, or is the pain spread throughout the area? And have you noticed if your left thigh looks any different from your right (such as swelling, looking larger, or any visible bump)?

“Doctor, the pain feels most intense in one spot on the left thigh, not the whole area, and it’s tender when I press there. I haven’t noticed any clear difference in size or any visible bump compared to my right thigh, just that spot hurts more and walking makes it worse.”

Is the pain specifically waking you up from sleep at night, or is it more that you can't fall asleep because of it? And is the pain constant even when you're resting, or does it mainly come with activity?
“Doctor, it’s waking me up—I’ll be resting and it still hurts, though it’s worse when I move. The pain feels pretty constant, but the activity makes it spike and that’s why I can’t get comfortable.”
Is the pain located in the upper part of your thigh near your hip, the middle of your thigh, or down toward your knee? And does the ibuprofen provide any relief at all, even temporarily?

“Doctor, it’s mainly in the middle to upper part of my left thigh, kind of toward my hip, and the ibuprofen doesn’t really help—if anything, it only eases it a little for a short time and then it comes back just as bad.”
Have you noticed if the skin over the painful area feels warmer than the other thigh, or if any veins look more prominent or visible on that side compared to your right leg?

“Doctor, I think that spot can feel a bit warmer than the other side, but I haven’t noticed any obvious visible veins or a clearly different appearance compared to my right leg. The main thing is that one tender point in the middle to upper left thigh hurts more and seems to be getting worse.”
